# Venture Dollars For Black Startup Founders Stay Scarce Despite AI Funding Boom (Crunchbase News)

By Mary Ann Azevedo. May 28, 2026.

## Key findings
- 2025: only ~$942M (0.32% of total U.S. venture funding) went to startups with a Black founder or co-founder — one of the lowest shares in years.
- 2026 (as of May 20): **$643M** raised by U.S. startups with a Black founder/co-founder; the majority in Q1 2026 — the most raised in a single quarter since Q2 2022 ($653M).
- The robust Q1 was driven largely by one outsized round: **SambaNova's February $350M Series E**. "Co-founded in 2017 by chief technologist **Kunle Olukotun**, the AI chip startup has raised a total of **$1.5 billion** in known funding. Cambium Capital Partners and Vista Equity Partners co-led its latest raise."
- Q1 2026 total came across just 34 deals (larger deal sizes).
- Standout 2026 Black-founder rounds: **SambaNova** (AI hardware/software; Intel increased stake to 8.2%); **Novig** (NY sweepstakes sports prediction market, $75M Series B led by Pantera at $500M post-money); **Harper** (SF AI-native insurance brokerage for SMBs, $47M Series A led by Emergence Capital, YC alum); **Posh** (live events, $37M Series B led by FirstMark); **GovDash** (AI-driven gov-contracting software, $30M Series B co-led by BCI and Mucker Capital).

## Assessment
- `authoritative: yes` — Crunchbase News is a recognized VC data outlet (Crunchbase DB) reporting its own Diversity Spotlight data.
- Confirms SambaNova as the dominant Black-founder AI round and names the other 2026 standouts. Used for Q5.1, Q5.2, Q5.7, Q5.8.
